title: Temporal-indicator decomposition across the irrigation forcing discontinuity

depends_on.RM16: the frozen 8.64 s raw dynamic-top solve converges
depends_on.RM17: dynamic FLUX and explicit qtop=-36 raw trajectories are bit-identical
depends_on.RM18: dynamic FLUX temporal certificate is available and equals the explicit-flux certificate
depends_on.RM19: the unchanged transaction is rejected by the inherited temporal budget with no unavailable-certificate rejection

question: Is the large RM19 temporal indicator primarily a local truncation defect within the new irrigation regime, or is it dominated by comparing the post-irrigation trajectory with a predecessor right derivative that belongs to the pre-irrigation forcing regime?
comparisons: No-irrigation full-window raw solve and temporal indicator with its same-regime predecessor derivative.
Irrigation full-window raw solve with the historical predecessor derivative used by the F-GC44 fixture.
Irrigation full-window raw solve with a post-switch origin derivative computed from the same Richards residual/operator at the accepted state under the new irrigation forcing.
Dynamic-FLUX and explicit-flux routes must remain numerically identical for every common predecessor derivative.

Direct full-window normalized indicator is compared with RM19 transaction max_temporal_indicator to determine whether the transaction diagnostic is the first-attempt value or a maximum over later retry attempts.
required_outputs: previous derivative infinity and mass-weighted norms
post-switch origin derivative infinity and mass-weighted norms
current secant derivative infinity and mass-weighted norms
hypotheses: The no-irrigation equilibrium-like trajectory has a temporal bound orders of magnitude below the irrigation-onset case.
Using the historical pre-irrigation predecessor reproduces the large RM18/RM19 onset defect.
Using the post-switch origin right derivative materially reduces the irrigation temporal bound if the dominant term is the forcing discontinuity rather than within-regime truncation.
Dynamic and explicit qtop=-36 certificates remain identical under the same predecessor.
No acceptance threshold or solver setting is needed to answer these diagnostic questions.
failure_rule: Do not alter HEAD_BUDGET, temporal tolerance, retry policy, irrigation forcing, raw solver tolerances or the temporal defect operator. A failure to reduce the bound with the post-switch derivative falsifies the forcing-discontinuity explanation.
nonclaims: RM20 does not authorize temporal-history reseeding.
RM20 does not alter accepted-state semantics.
RM20 does not admit a new temporal budget.
RM20 does not admit the three-model triangle.
A post-switch derivative may only become production state after a separate prospective contract and rollback/restart qualification.
